# Fireplace Contributor License Agreement

Thank you for helping build Fireplace. This agreement lets the project use your contribution safely and for the long term. **You keep ownership of what you write.** You give the project the permissions below so that it can keep distributing the app, now and in the future.

By agreeing, you accept these terms for every contribution you submit to the Fireplace project from the date you agree. You can agree once, by following the steps at the end.

## 1. Words used here
- **Fireplace** means the open-source project maintained under the GitHub organisation `fireplacechat`, and the people who maintain it. It also means any successor: a legal entity, such as a non-profit organisation, to which the project is transferred.
- **You** means the person agreeing. If you contribute as part of a job or for an organisation, it also means that organisation, and the person agreeing must be authorised to speak for it.
- **Contribution** means any code, text, image, design or other work that you submit to Fireplace (for example in a pull request, issue or discussion), including changes to existing work.

Fireplace may also license your Contribution to others under other terms, including commercial terms, as long as the public version stays available under that open-source licence.

## 3. Patent licence
You grant Fireplace and everyone who receives the project a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, free of charge, royalty-free, irrevocable patent licence to make, have made, use, sell, offer to sell, import and otherwise transfer your Contribution, but only for patents you own or control that your Contribution on its own, or combined with the project, necessarily infringes. If you start a patent lawsuit claiming that the project or a Contribution infringes your patent, the licence you granted under this section for that project ends on the day you file.

## 4. You keep your rights
This is a licence, not a transfer of ownership. You can still use, publish and license your own Contribution in any other way you like.

## 5. What you promise
You confirm that:
1. You have the right to grant the licences above. If your employer or anyone else has rights in your work, you have their permission, or they have waived those rights for this Contribution.
2. Your Contribution is your own original work, or you have said clearly, in the pull request, which parts come from elsewhere and under what licence.
3. If you used an AI tool, you reviewed the result, you understand it, and you are not knowingly submitting material that is copied from someone else or that you have no right to share.
4. Your Contribution contains no passwords, keys, recovery codes, real people's messages or other private data.

## 6. Other people's work
If you include or build on material from someone else, say so in the pull request, name the source and its licence, and do not include it if its licence is incompatible with the AGPL-3.0.

## 7. As is
Your Contribution is provided as it is, without warranties or conditions of any kind. You do not have to provide support. Fireplace does not have to accept or merge any Contribution.

## 8. Telling us if something changes
If you learn that anything in section 5 was or has become untrue, please tell the maintainers promptly (see `SECURITY.md` for private contact).

## 9. Successors
Fireplace may transfer its rights under this agreement to a successor as described in section 1, and the successor may use them in the same way.

## 10. Stopping
You can stop agreeing to this for **future** contributions at any time by telling the maintainers. Licences you already granted for contributions you have already submitted stay in place, so that the project can keep distributing them.

## How to agree
Open the signatures issue linked in the pull request check, and post exactly this comment from your GitHub account:

> I have read the Fireplace Contributor License Agreement and I agree to its terms.

One comment covers all your future contributions. The comment, your GitHub account and the date are the record. If you contribute for an organisation, post it from an account authorised to act for that organisation and name the organisation in the same comment.
